newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen hiking rates before late summer-Goldstein.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen hiking rates before late summer-Goldstein.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to raise short-term interest rates at least one more time before the end of the summer, said Ken Goldstein, an economist at The Conference Board.

"Between now and the end of the summer, certainly between now and the end of the year, we are going to get at least one -- probably more than one -- increase in interest rates," said Goldstein without detailing the exact amount of the possible rate hike(s).

Goldstein spoke to Reuters Financial Television after the Conference Board released its consumer confidence index, which posted a 28-year high at 127.1 in May. The index was revised to 118.5 in April, The Conference Board said.
Additionally, Golstein said the American workers' fears of corporate downsizing seem to be over, giving them more confidence about their jobs and spending.

"What we are really seeing here is the American working consumer has finally gotten over the fear of downsizing and has finally realized that this is a strong economy and it is not breaking up," Goldstein said, adding that "(consumers) are beginning to enjoy it -- not only in jobs but in terms of their spending."
